meta.notes: Arcade tenants' counsel. Commissioned the deed copy for the Arcade's rent and read it for that. Sharp about money, slow about envelopes. Stops at what a paper shows.

threads.topic: Does your clerk's book agree with the Ortiz boy's?
threads.source: Kept from a cut chain. Proves the book where the letter needs it.

ew_1.line: Ten o'clock, with Miss Quell. Nobody cancelled. Well. Somebody did. I had this on Saturday from upstairs over there, on her good paper, telling me I need not attend. "The person who kept the counter." I've had forty years of landlords and that's the rudest thing that has ever arrived on time.

ew_2.line: Her copy of my deed. She wanted to show Miss Quell something in the schedule, and she was very pleased about it, and now I'll never know what it was. I do Arcade rents. I read a schedule the way you read a bus.

ew_3.line: It's on my file with its envelope. My clerk pins everything. If he had pinned my wife's letters I'd be a happier man. Come to the office if you've a reason.

ew_n1.line: On the Saturday, by the first post. Telling me I need not attend, about a woman I had already heard was dead from a boy with a bicycle. "The person who kept the counter." I've had forty years of landlords. It's on my file with its envelope.

ew_n2.line: My clerk pins everything. I have asked him not to. It is the only reason I know what my wife wrote me in 1911.

ew_l1.line: Who's been letting the maintenance read schedules? It means when the Kessler lease on that lot ends, the lot comes back to the Arcade's ground. First of August, this one. After that, I'd want to know on what authority anybody was collecting.

choices.label: So the tenants don't owe her.

ew_l2.line: Then you have a receipt, which shows she collected. Whether she was entitled is a question for a court and not for a receipt. Don't look at me like that. I charge for the other answer.

ew_l3.line: I said no such thing, and neither did you, if anyone asks.

ew_lt1.line: Stamped received, July twentieth, eight-fifty. Pinned. Why would I turn... that's a pencil. "C.O., 6.40." That's the Ortiz boy, he marks anything he holds. Six-forty when?

choices.label: His book says Friday. Six-forty, Friday the nineteenth.

ew_lt2.line: Friday. She was up on that roof at six-forty on Friday with a camera. I saw her buy the sandwich. This says last night's storm. Sit down. No. I'll sit down. I have had that on my file for a long time, as bad manners.

ew_t1.line: My clerk stamps what this office takes, and the Ortiz boy pencils what he holds. Bring the book, sit there, read me the summer. Sixty-odd pieces, and not a minute between them that I could bill for. In a witness I would call that a fault. I looked.
